content:
Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark. While it has its own government and considerable self-governing powers, Denmark retains authority over certain areas, such as foreign affairs and defense.

The right to govern Greenland is therefore shared between the local government, which handles internal matters including education, health, and infrastructure, and the Danish government, which manages broader issues. This arrangement is established under the Greenland Self-Government Act, which came into effect in 2009, granting Greenland a high degree of self-rule while still being part of the Kingdom of Denmark.
